bio: Professor at Universidade Estadual do Tocantins, where she leads the Research Group on Development and Environmental Performance. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Engineering, a Master’s degree in Agroecosystems, and a Ph.D. in Regional Development. She has been a Visiting Researcher at the Institute of Management and Strategy, University of St. Gallen, Switzerland. She has provided consultancy to the Ministry of the Environment of Brazil and the Inter-American Institute for Cooperation on Agriculture. She is a board member of the State Council for Water Resources in Brazil, Ambassador of the Climate Solutions Simulator of MIT, and board member of Metaphorum and the American Society for Cybernetics. Her work focuses on applying the Viable System Model (VSM) to complex adaptive systems, particularly in water governance.

CEO of The Infinite Game and systems thinker with a background in telecommunications, control systems engineering, and organizational design. Former Chief Research Scientist at BT and Project Supervisor at the University of Cambridge and the University of Oxford. Senior Researcher at Khalifa University and Lecturer at the University of Northumbria. Developer of the Ibex Identity Model and frameworks integrating surprise metabolism, recursive closure, and cybernetic stewardship. Chartered Engineer (CEng) and Honorary Fellow of The Cybernetics Society.

affiliation: University of Exeter / De Montfort University
bio: Honorary Senior Lecturer at the University of Exeter and Programme Director at De Montfort University (Cambodia). Consultant and researcher in complexity in management, with previous roles at Leeds Beckett University and Cranfield University. His work focuses on complexity management in strategy, security, sustainability, innovation, and management systems inspired by co-evolving and transition management principles. He has led projects across the UK, Europe, Latin America, and Cambodia.

Director of Metaphorum and organizational cybernetics scholar. She earned her PhD in organizational cybernetics in 1995 and worked closely with Stafford Beer. Former Reader in Cybernetics at Hull University Business School and currently an Emeritus Fellow. Honorary Research Fellow at Exeter University and Transylvania Executive Education. Recipient of the Ashby Lecture (2002) and Norbert Wiener Award (2006). Author of books including 'A Complexity Approach to Sustainability' and 'Sustainable Self-governance in Businesses and Societies: The Viable System Model in Action'.

Jon Walker has over forty years experience working in the co-operative business sector establishing and developing democratically run enterprises . He has established and co-managed a range of businesses including retail outlets, a small-scale manufacturing plant, a warehouse and a chain of supermarkets dealing mainly with wholefood, organic and fairly-traded products. Concurrently, Jon has lectured, published, consulted and provided training courses in both private and public sectors, on organisational structures. In particular Jon has pioneered the use of innovative organisational techniques based on the Viable Systems Model, in large cooperatives, and with Angela Espinosa in eco-community, a network of schools and a hospital. The resulting organisational changes have resulted in working practices which are both efficient whilst at the same time being based on principles of participation and individual creativity and autonomy.

Lecturer in Management Studies and Operational Disaster Management at the University of Manchester. He holds a PhD in Business and Management (Operations Management) from Alliance Manchester Business School and an MSc from the University of Warwick. His research focuses on enhancing resilience, agility, and viability of systems during emergencies, particularly managing spontaneous volunteers in disasters, using VSM, SSM, and systems thinking methodologies.

Principal at Cwarel Isaf Institute and independent consultant based in Toronto. She worked with Stafford Beer from the early 1980s until his death in 2002. Former President of Metaphorum, the American Society for Cybernetics, and the International Society for Systems Science. She applies cybernetic approaches including the Viable System Model, Team Syntegrity, and Operations Room design in nonprofit and business organizations.

Professor at the University of Valladolid specializing in system dynamics and organizational cybernetics. Creator of the VSMod® software supporting the Viable System Model. Former Director of International Relations at the University of Valladolid (2000–2006). Author of over 80 publications and five books, including 'Design and Diagnosis for Sustainable Organizations: The Viable System Method'. Recipient of the Kybernetes Research Award (2006) and Honorary HSSS Award as Distinguished Scientist (2007). Board member of the World Organization of Systems and Cybernetics and Fellow of HSSS.

Constantin leads the Malik Group in Switzerland as co-owner and co-CEO, where he helps organizations with some of society's most complex challenges—from climate adaptation and public health transformation to reimagining how governments can serve their citizens more effectively. For 20 years, he has worked alongside cities, research institutions, and international corporations to design systems that are resilient, equitable, and capable of evolving with our rapidly changing world. His approach draws on cybernetics and systems science to help leaders see beyond immediate crises and build capacity for long-term transformation. Constantin's academic background spans law, psychology, and business sustainability management. He is a member of the International Society for the Systems Sciences and the American Society for Cybernetics. His book, Ahead of Change, explores how crowd psychology and cybernetics might transform democratic decision-making—offering a glimpse of more adaptive governance for the 21st century. He believes the solutions to our greatest challenges emerge not from single interventions, but from understanding and reshaping the systems that shape our lives.

An attorney (Universidad del Rosario - Colombia). He holds a doctorate and master's degree in Ethics and Democracy from the University of Valencia (Spain), master’s degrees in economics (National University of Colombia) and in Political Science (IAEE - Madrid). His research lines focus on truth studies and peacebuilding, as well as organizational cybernetics applied to law and public administration. Serves as an arbitrator at the Arbitration Centers of the Chambers of Commerce of Bogotá, Barranquilla, Cartagena, and Pereira. Within the Council of State of Colombia, he has held the positions of President, Magistrate of the Consultation and Civil Service Chamber, and Ad Hoc Justice of the Council of State. He has served as Minister of Education, as well as Deputy Comptroller General of the Republic of Colombia, Ambassador to Venezuela, and Director of the World Center for Research and Training in Conflict Resolution. An active member of WOSC, the Colombian Academy of Jurisprudence, the Ibero-American Forum of Administrative Law (FIDA), and the Franco-Colombian Association of Jurists (AJFC). Author of some books and papers. He serves as a reviewer for international   journals.  During his professional career he was a professor at several universities, international lecturer, organizational consultant, and litigator.

A practising consultant cybernetician since 1990. An experienced Board Chair and Non-Executive Director with a focus on developing strategic and operational adaptation and transformation rooted in cybernetic reasoning. His approach seeks to enhance performance through new insights and thoughtful innovation, working especially with organisations facing challenges of adaptation, survival and growth. Leadership built on effective mentoring enables his coherent whole system approach synthesising the three dimensions of people, process and information. His experience extends across public, private and 3rd sector , includeinginfrastructure, energy, transport, housing, criminal justice, social care, health care and both service focused and manufacturing organisations. Partner in Beckford Consulting, Chair of Corehaus Ltd (MMC housing), Visiting Professor at University College London and at Loughborough University Business School . Until April 2025, he was Board Chair at Rise Mutual CIC (Domestic Abuse, VAWG) and NED at Fusion21 Ltd. (2014-2023). Currently co-supervising 3 doctoral students researching data driven decision making and 3 researching long term effectiveness of interventions with perpetrators of domestic abuse/VAWG. PhD in Management Systems and Sciences (Hull). Fellow and past President of the Cybernetics Society, Member of The Institute of Management Services, Fellow of the RSA and Fellow of the Institute of Engineering and Technology.

Markus Schwaninger is a Professor Emeritus at the Institute of Management and Strategy, University of St. Gallen (Switzerland). Research focus: Organizational intelligence, corporate transformation and learning, systemic issues of sustainability. Methodological orientation: Systems approaches; emphasis: Organizational Cybernetics (Viable Systems, Variety Engineering), System Dynamics.  Studies in Economics, Sociology and Management at Universities in Austria (Salzburg, Innsbruck), Switzerland (St. Gallen) and France (Aix-Marseille). Habilitation and venia legendi at the University of St. Gallen, Switzerland (UNISG). Memberships: WOSC-World Organization of Systems and Cybernetics (advisory board), International Academy of Cybernetics and Systems, System Dynamics Society, ISSS-International Society for the Systems Sciences, GWS-Gesellschaft für Wirtschafts- und Sozialkybernetik, BSSS-Bertalanffy Center for the Study of Systems Science (Fellow). Markus has researched, lectured and consulted internationally. Research residencies abroad: MIT-Massachusetts Institute of Technology, U.S.A.; Columbia University, U.S.A.; UBC-University of British Columbia, Canada; Fundação Getúlio Vargas, Brazil; Universidad de los Andes, Colombia; Instituto Tecnológico da Aeronáutica, Brazil. Founder of the System Dynamics Group at the Institute of Management and Strategy, UNISG. Publishing: Long-standing Managing Editor of the System Dynamics Review. His publications amount to roughly 250, in six languages, including 15 books.

affiliation: World Organization of Systems and Cybernetics
bio: President of the World Organization of Systems and Cybernetics (WOSC) and Director of Syncho Research, UK. An academician of the International Academy for Systems and Cybernetic Sciences (IASCYS) and Past Professor of Systems and Cybernetics at the University of Lincoln, UK. His research is in organisational cybernetics and systems. His most referred book is “Organizational Systems: Managing Complexity with the Viable System Model”, 2011 in English and 2016 in Spanish (both with A. Reyes). Has co-published five books and edited 7 special issues of journals, most significantly in 2018 “Futures of Society: the interactions revolution” in Futures. Has published over a 120 papers in journals and books. Has organised and co-organised four of WOSC’s  World Congresses, with Alfonso Reyes in the University of Ibague, Colombia, in 2014, with Sergio Barile in La Sapienza University of Rome, Italy, in 2017, with Vladimir Lepskiy and Igor Perko, virtually from Moscow in 2021, with Igor Perko in the University of Oxford in 2023.  In June 2024 he was awarded by ASC the Norbert Wiener medal. From 1971 to 1973 he was operations director of the CYBERSYN project - for the Chilean Government  under the scientific direction of Professor Stafford Beer.

A nomad, having previously lived a variety of lifes as a practitioner and academic. Currently at Centre for Systems Engineering in Department of Space and Climate Physics (MSSL) at University College London.  Practitioner experience spans the coal, oil, electronics and tourism industries, in roles that have included manager, director and consultant. Expertise lies in managing organisational transformation (e.g. business recovery, strategic positioning, technology implementation). Awarded a PhD in 2010 from the University of Edinburgh Business School for developing a conceptual explanation (‘domestication’) for how people take up and use online technologies. This has provided a platform to develop a research portfolio that operates at the intersection of technology, sustainability and social complexity. This work is grounded in the conceptual insights of Cybersystemics. and the Sociology of Technology. Stephen’s growing portfolio of publications includes a book, journal, conference and working papers, online journalist articles and evidence to UK Parliament.

Space entrepreneur and PhD candidate in Space Sciences and Technologies at the Aeronautics Institute of Technology (ITA) in Brazil, Visiting Researcher at the Politecnico di Milano (PoliMi). His doctoral research examines the dynamic governance of emerging space ecosystems by integrating Stafford Beer’s Viable System Model (VSM) with organizational process theory.

Emeritus Professor at the University of Hull and MD of Systems Research Ltd. He graduated from Oxford University, gained an MA from Lancaster University and a PhD from Hull, and has worked in the civil service, in academia and as a consultant. Between 1999 and 2011, Mike was Dean of Hull University Business School, leading it to triple-crown accreditation. Has been President of the International Federation for Systems Research and the International Society for the Systems Sciences. He was editor-in-chief of Systems Research and Behavioral Science for 26 years. In 2011 was awarded an OBE for services to higher education and business. In 2017 received the Beale Medal of the UK Operational Research Society for ‘a sustained contribution over many years to the theory, practice, and philosophy of Operational Research’. In 2022 received the Pioneer Award of the International Council on Systems Engineering for ‘the development of the foundations of systems engineering as author, educator and intellectual leader in systems thinking’. Known as a key figure in the development of ‘critical systems thinking’ - a topic on which he has published ten books and over 150 articles. His latest book Critical Systems Thinking: A Practitioner’s Guide was published in 2024.

affiliation: ConCriterio Market Innovation Think Lab, Colombia
bio: Researcher, consultant, and university professor with over 25 years of experience in applied market research, innovation management, and strategic analysis across diverse economic sectors. Founder and Director of ConCriterio — a marketing innovation think lab supporting markets transformation, sustainability, and mission-oriented innovation processes. My work integrates rigorous mixed-method approaches — deep qualitative inquiry, social network analysis, bibliometrics, systems modeling, spatial analysis, and data science — to understand markets as complex socio-technical systems. I translate empirical and scientific evidence into strategic decisions, contributing to sustainable market formation, transformative innovation, and alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Currently a PhD Candidate in Technology and Innovation Management (UPB, EAFIT scholarship), with a thesis focused on transformative exchange for socio-technical system transitions.

Captain Jonathan Huxley PhD (RFA Rtd) is a retired officer from the Royal Fleet Auxiliary. He has spent 47 years at sea from the age of 17, ofwhich 24 were in command as a qualified Master Mariner with Polar Navigation endorsement and specialist Royal Navy Navigation Instructor and SRN4 Hovercraft Navigator. During his career he has worked in a wide variety of theatres from the Atlantic, North America, Mediterranean, Persian Gulf, Sierra Leone, Indian Ocean, Far East, Australasia, Pacific, South Atlantic, Antarctic, South America, and Arctic. Undertaking amphibious operations, afloat support, maritime security, defence engagement, MCM support, aviation, submarine support and special operations. As well as command at sea Captain Huxley has been actively involved in participating in strategic, personnel and change management, developing strategies, implementing change programmes, negotiating with Maritime Trade Unions and interfacing with programmes, negotiating with Maritime Trade Unions and interfacing with government organisations such as the Treasury. His focus during all this work has been examining how groups organise themselves and make decisions. He conducted research into the viability of salient social identities for his doctorate and continues his research studies into group behaviour.

Roelien Goede is the Director of the Unit of Data Science and Computing at North-West University, South Africa, and a Past-President of the International Society of Systems Sciences.  Her research interest is Critical Systems Thinking applied to Business Intelligence. She is an independent assessor for the L7 ST apprenticeship in the UK. She has been involved as a systems specialist in various international projects and frequently presents workshops and keynote addresses on Critical Systems Heuristics. She has published in journals such as Systemic Practice and Action Research, Systems Research and Behavioural Science (SRBS), Journal of Transdisciplinary Studies, and Communications of the Association for Computing Machinery (ACM) and the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) on Computer and Information Science. She is the section editor for Critical Systems Thinking of the SRBS. She holds a PhD in Information Technology from the University of Pretoria, South Africa. Her PhD focus was on Systems Thinking in Decision Support Systems. She has supervised 14 PhD students and 16 Master’s students. She is recognised by the South African Research Foundation as a scholar with considerable international recognition for the high quality and impact of her work.

Gary Smith is a Senior Expert in systems engineering and architecture within the aerospace, defence and security sector, and a Past-President of the International Society for the Systems Sciences. He is also Section Editor for Foundations of Systems Engineering in the Systems Engineering Body of Knowledge (SEBoK). His professional practice spans systems engineering, enterprise and mission architecture, organisational transformation, and integrated business management systems. His interests include systems science, methodological pluralism, organisational cybernetics, system dynamics, Soft Systems Methodology, and the relationship between systems thinking and systems engineering. Gary’s research explores meta-frameworks for organising transversal knowledge about systems, relationships among form, function and fit, and systemic coherence in human-AI collaboration. He is a guest editor for work bringing systems thinking and systems biology into closer dialogue. He contributes regularly to international systems communities, conferences and collaborative research initiatives, seeking to connect foundational systems theory with practical challenges in organisations, engineering, health and society.

Jeremy Pryce holds a first degree in International Relations and has worked across professional sport, education, organisational development, and community-based projects. A former professional athlete, he has spent much of his later work exploring how sport, education, and civic participation can support human development and social belonging. He currently leads Projekt Bergsjön, an initiative supported by Allmänna Arvsfonden and IFK Göteborg Friidrott, focused on participation, belonging, and community-based development through sport. He also serves on the advisory board for Frihamnsdagarna in Gothenburg, a civic platform for democracy and public dialogue. His current work explores how systems preserve, distort, or lose contact with their foundational purpose under pressure. He is developing two related lines of inquiry: ontological foundations for ethical and regenerative viable systems, and Incentive Gravity as a framework for understanding institutional drift, distributed responsibility, and behavioural tendency within complex systems. His interest in Stafford Beer and the Viable System Model comes from a practical concern with how governance, feedback, identity, and purpose can help systems remain adaptive without losing ethical orientation.

When the Internet was still in its infancy, Uruguay experienced a groundbreaking technological transformation as it reestablished its democracy. The URUguay CIBernético project (Cybernetic Uruguay, or URUCIB) emerged as a cutting-edge, real-time information system designed to enhance government decision-making. This visionary initiative sets the stage for future innovations in data management and has since been adopted by multiple countries, underscoring its lasting impact. Led by Víctor Ganón, this pioneering project operated during the presidency of Julio María Sanguinetti from 1985 to 1990 and was developed under the expertise of the esteemed English cybernetician Professor Stafford Beer. Ganón, an Industrial Engineer from Universidad de la República (UDELAR) with specializations in Communications and Electronics, also holds a degree in Computer Management Studies from the University of London. As a co-main author of the 'Sistema de información ejecutivo URUCIB' software, Ganón held the position of national director of URUCIB, under Project URU/86/004, 'Informática para la Presidencia de la República' from 1986 to 1990. In the private sector, he is the founding partner of QUANAM, a prominent information technology professional services firm established in 1976.

Cristina Cervino is a Ph.D. student at the Department of Economics, Management, and Institutions (DEMI), University of Naples “Federico II,” Italy. She currently serves as the Secretary of ASVSA (Associazione per la Ricerca sui Sistemi Vitali) and is also a member of WOSC (World Organization of Systems and Cybernetics). She has participated in several international conferences in the fields of knowledge management, sustainability reporting and systems thinking, contributing as a peer reviewer. Her academic identity is grounded in the Viable Systems Approach.

affiliation: Department of Social Anthropology, Panteion University, Athens
bio: Postdoctoral researcher in the Department of Social Anthropology at Panteion University. The title of my research is 'The entropic control societies and the invention of democratic algorithmic machines of negentropy'. Recently completed the construction of a map of Liberty AI Machines through the articulation of Viable System Model, Schizoanalysis. LAIMs are configured by the cooperation of experts and non-experts to provide an ecosophic eudemonic ethos in the institutions through the warm instead big datafication. I am a member of the Metaphorum cooperative, as well as the Society of Deleuze and Guattari Studies Athens. Still active on social movements regarding Commons, Direct Democracy and Social Ecology.I have translated, under a commons license in Greek, the 'Precarious Rhapsody - Semiocapitalism and the pathologies of post-alpha generation'  by Franco Berardi Bifo and 'The Beginning of History Value Struggles and Global Capital'  by Massimo De Angelis, as well as many articles regarding commons, feminism, social ecology and heterarchical movements. I am passionate about creating a barefoot cybernetics perspective by and for all earthlings.

Taja Maček is a PhD candidate at the Faculty of Tourism Studies – Turistica, University of Primorska, and an experienced tourism professional specialising in cruise tourism and destination management. Her research focuses on sustainable cruise shorescapes through the application of systems thinking and system dynamics, with particular attention to stakeholder relationships, destination governance, corporate social responsibility, and sustainable shore-excursion development.

Tadeja Jere Jakulin is Full Professor of Systems Theory in Tourism at the University of Primorska, Faculty of Tourism Studies – Turistica (Portorož, Slovenia), where she serves as Vice Dean for Internationalisation and Quality and heads the Department of Cultural Tourism. She is President of the Slovenian Society for Systems Research and a member of the  AIEST (International Association of Scientific Experts in Tourism). Her research applies general systems theory, systems thinking, cybernetics, and system dynamics to tourism, cultural heritage, and pilgrimage. In her latest research, she began working with the Viable System Model, the Object–Subject–Model epistemological triad, and Peircean semiotics, using the Škofjeloški pasijon -Slovenia's UNESCO-listed passion play -as an empirical case. At Metaphorum 2026, she examines how the VSM illuminates the governance and long-term viability of this living heritage performance. She has published in Kybernetes, PLOS ONE,  Sensors, Brain Sciences and the International Journal of Religious Tourism and Pilgrimage, with chapters for Routledge, Palgrave Macmillan, Springer, and Edward Elgar. She co-edited Law, Humanities, and Tourism (Cambridge Scholars, 2026) and received the 2026 IRTP Lifetime Achievement Award.

Mateus van Stralen is a practicing architect and lecturer at the Architecture School of the Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais (UFMG), where he has been a faculty member since 2015. There, he is a researcher at Lagear (Graphics Laboratory for Architectural Experience) and at NEXT (Experimentation Center in Digital Technologies), where he investigates the use of digital technologies for training, learning, design, and urbanism. He is also a director at Kubus4D, a studio exploring the use of computation in architecture, and a member at large of the Executive Committee of the American Society for Cybernetics. In his work, the circularity between acting and understanding is structured from a cybernetic perspective, which forms the basis for the general conceptual framework to explore and understand the systemic nature of architecture. Mateus' research interests address design education, architecture, computational design, and Second-Order Cybernetics, intertwining theory and practice.

Jose S. Cabral Filho is an architect and a semi-retired professor at the School of Architecture at the Federal University of Minas Gerais (Brazil). His research focuses on the liberating potential of technology, seeking a far-reaching adoption of play in digital design, using games as a framework for the coexistence of determinism and non-determinism. His main interests include the philosophy of Vilém Flusser, Second-Order Cybernetics, as well as architectural-performance and electronic music.

Andreas Slogar is an experter in management cybernetics and AI-centred enterprise transformation, as well as the author of numerous specialist articles, podcasts, and the books “The agile Organisation” (Hanser, 2018, 2020), “Liquid Leadership – Management Handbook for self-organized cooperation” (Schäffer-Poeschel, 2024) and ”Handbook agile Transformation” (Schäffer-Poeschel, 2025). He is also a speaker, keynote presenter, podcaster and curator at numerous international conferences.

Ricardo is a designer, artist, programmer and cultural manager. Ricardo holds MFA Design and Technology (Parsons, The New School), with studies in Information Visualisation and Data Science. He is a professor at the School of Design, and has taught at the School of Engineering, both at Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile (PUC).  He directs the UC Design Data Visualisation Diploma. He is interested in transdisciplinary links, carrying out studies in Philosophy and Sciences. He develops projects at the intersection between visualization, graphics, programming, art and design, exploring the aesthetic representation of data. He is the founder of C80.cl, a project that, since 2015 has used visualisations to support the contextualized understanding of the Chilean Constitution of 1980. He founded Artnumerica.info, oriented to algorithmic design and data visualization. As an artist, he has participated in exhibitions, conferences and presentations in Chile, Argentina, Brazil, Spain, and Estonia. Currently, he is pursuing a PhD in Computational Engineering (double degree) at PUC (Chile) & University of Edinburgh (Scotland).

Vijaya Manchem is an independent systems practitioner with interests in systems thinking, and organisational design. Her current work focuses on how Stafford Beer’s Viable System Model can be applied within educational organisations through digital platforms, enabling organisational structures and management processes to operate more coherently in practice. Drawing on experience across the education sector, including apprenticeship provision, curriculum design, governance, and quality assurance, she is interested in the practical challenges of translating systemic concepts into everyday practice. Vijaya holds an MSc in Engineering, a Postgraduate Certificate in Academic Practice (PGCAP), and a Diploma in Leadership and Management, together with professional qualifications in auditing, assessment, and quality assurance.

Steve Outtrim is co-founder and CEO of Dynamic Experts. He first studied the Viable System Model as an undergraduate at Victoria University of Wellington in 1992 and applied its principles to the structure of his first company, Sausage Software, creator of HotDog, one of the most widely downloaded Internet applications of the dot-com era, which he founded at 23 and grew to a peak market capitalization of $1.2 billion. Three decades later he returned to Beer's model as the control architecture for autonomous AI agents, fused with David Teece's Dynamic Capabilities framework: the Viable Agentic System.

David J. Teece is Professor of the Graduate School at the University of California, Berkeley, Distinguished Scholar of Strategy and Innovation at the University of South Florida’s Muma College of Business, Chairman Emeritus of the Berkeley Research Group, and co-founder and Executive Chairman of Dynamic Experts. He received his PhD in economics from the University of Pennsylvania in 1975, during Stafford Beer’s adjunct professorship at the Wharton School. A scholar-entrepreneur, Professor Teece is best known for originating the Dynamic Capabilities framework, the Dynamic Competition paradigm, and the Profiting from Innovation model, which have shaped research and practice in strategy, innovation, entrepreneurship, and competition policy. His work has been cited more than 269,000 times, making him one of the world's most influential scholars in business and economics. He advises governments and corporations worldwide on strategy, innovation, and technological change. In 2020, Clarivate ranked him the world's most influential scholar in management and named him a Clarivate Laureate in Economics for his contributions to innovation, entrepreneurship, and competition. In 2021, Thinkers50 recognized him as a Distinguished Management Thinker.

Thomas McEvoy-Zafiropulos is a PhD candidate in Cybernetics at the Australian National University. He holds previous degrees in philosophy and quantitative economics, and his research explores the self, existentialism, and psychopathology through cybernetics. Born in Chile, Thomas has long been interested in Stafford Beer’s intellectual and practical legacy, particularly his engagement with Latin America and the philosophical implications of his work.

PhD Candidate in Systems Engineering at Instituto Politécnico Nacional, Mexico. Her research focuses on Systems Thinking, complex systems, water governance and the dynamics of tourism systems from a transdisciplinary perspective. Her work centres on the study and design of social-ecological systems through the application of methodologies such as the Viable System Model, Soft Systems Methodology and System Dynamics to address challenges related to sustainability and governance. She has published scientific articles in JCR indexed and international journals, as well as book chapters on tourism, sustainability and Systems Thinking. She has presented her research at international conferences, including Metaphorum (Berlin and Manchester) and ISSS (Washington and Birmingham), as well as at several national events, including the International Congress on Applied Tourism Research and the Mexican Academy of Tourism Research. She is a member of Grupo de Investigación en Sistémica y Turismo. Her research integrates Systems Thinking with territorial action to contribute to the design of governance strategies and regenerative solutions for rural communities.

Isaías Badillo-Piña holds a degree in Electrical Engineering and earned both his Master's and PhD degrees in Systems Engineering. He has published more than 30 research articles in JCR indexed (Q1 and Q2) and Scopus indexed journals, as well as more than 15 book chapters with internationally recognised academic publishers. He is a Research Professor in the PhD Programme in Systems Engineering at Instituto Politécnico Nacional, Mexico. His research focuses on Systems Science. He has led more than 5 research projects and has supervised 5 doctoral theses and 4 master's dissertations. He is a member of several prestigious professional and academic associations, including the Asociación Mexicana de Ingenieros Mecánicos y Electricistas, the College of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, the Mexican Institute of Systems and Cybernetics, the Mexican Academy of Systems Science, the Asociación Latinoamericana de Sistemas (Secretary, 2008–2010), the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), the ISSS, and the American Production and Inventory Control Society (APICS).

Richard Gunther is an independent practitioner based in Newcastle, County Down, and the founder of Recursive Systems, where he develops software for organisational diagnosis using Stafford Beer's Viable System Model. The system treats model output as provisional: structure goes onto the map only when it passes an evidence-gated test, and unresolved gaps become diagnostic questions rather than invented answers. He has tested this workflow on two public-record cases. Alongside this work he advises manufacturers on Amazon marketplace strategy and builds the software supporting that practice, which is where his interest in applying the VSM to real organisational problems began. He studied Management Science at Bayes Business School in London, with periods in Hong Kong and Austin, and first encountered the VSM in an undergraduate dissertation on virtual organisations. His next step is testing it with practitioners in a live organisation, and he hopes to meet people willing to challenge the method.

affiliation: Canadian Centre for the Study of Co-operatives
bio: Marc-André Pigeon is the director of the Canadian Centre for the Study of Co-operatives and an assistant professor in the Johnson Shoyama Graduate School of Public Policy (JSGS).  His research interests center around the study of co-operatives, governance, and money and banking. In relation to this line of inquiry, Dr. Pigeon has of late been exploring the intersection of cybernetics, co-operative governance and public policy. Prior to joining the JSGS, Dr. Pigeon worked as the assistant vice president of financial sector policy at the Canadian Credit Union Association, where he was responsible for monitoring, researching and advocating on behalf of credit unions.  He has also served as an advisor at the Department of Finance, a lead analyst for two major Parliamentary committees (Senate Banking, Trade and Commerce; House of Commons Finance), an economist at the Levy Economics Institute, and a business reporter for Bloomberg Business News. Dr. Pigeon holds a PhD from Carleton University in mass communications, a master’s degree in economics from the University of Ottawa, and a journalism degree from Carleton University. Dr. Pigeon has served on several non-profit and charitable boards, including the Co-operative Development Foundation (CDF), the Saskatchewan Co-operative Association, and Saskatoon Unitarians. In his spare time, he enjoys all-season camping with his family and their dog Pepsi and volunteering as a mechanic at Bridge City Bicycle Co-operative.

Nour Abida is an award-winning journalist, documentary filmmaker and systems thinking practitioner working at the intersection of journalism, organisational design and public service media. With more than a decade of experience in international broadcasting, she has led editorial and strategic projects spanning digital transformation, global audience engagement and organisational change. Alongside her work in journalism, Nour is completing an MSc in Systems Thinking in Practice at the University of Exeter, where she explores how systems methodologies including Stafford Beer’s Viable System Model, Soft Systems Methodology and Critical Systems Heuristics can help media organisations navigate complexity, strengthen resilience and improve decision-making. Her research focuses on applying systems thinking to contemporary challenges in public service media, including organisational viability, podcast discovery, audience trust and inclusive journalism. Nour is particularly interested in how diversity contributes to organisational resilience through Ashby’s Law of Requisite Variety and how cybernetic thinking can inform the future of journalism in an increasingly complex world. Nour was named Best Journalist at the 2025 Forty Under Forty Awards. Her documentary The Homecoming reached more than four million viewers and has been screened internationally, including at Columbia University, the University of Oxford and the Africa Centre.

Marcus Barrick is an independent scholar, musician and systems engineer whose work explores how Process Philosophy, Enactive Cognitive Science, Cybernetics, and Socioeconomic Systems can be integrated to better understand and cultivate Collective Agency. Drawing on a background in Engineering Physics and experience in simulation engineering, his research seeks to bridge technical, philosophical, and organizational perspectives through a process-relational understanding of agency. His current work develops the Enactive Viable Agency (EVA) framework, which synthesizes Stafford Beer's Viable System Model with insights from enactivism and meta-cybernetics to provide a practical grammar for interpreting and operationalizing viable systems. Marcus is also the author of the forthcoming book Healing Fragmentation: Enacting Socioeconomic Systems Change Through Process Philosophy and Cognitive Science, which explores pathways toward more resilient, participatory, and life-affirming institutions.

German-born social scientist living in Sweden, with an academic background in sociology and anthropology. For introducing me to cybernetics, I owe thanks to Dan Davies putting forward a view of organizations as substantively lifelike and intelligent that clicked for me. Coming up academically during covid has coloured my approach greatly, as I often think about systems with an eye to crisis and disaster. My current fields of interest are Scandinavian labour relations, reflexivity and feedback in recommender systems, and understanding ovelapping systems/ecosystems. I am here of my own volition, in that I am institutionally unaffiliated, and welcome all offers to change that. In the spirit of sufficient communications channels, you can find me on linkedin at https://www.linkedin.com/in/franzspengler/ .

Professor of Useful Art at Liverpool John Moores University's School of Art and Creative Industries. He has spent over two decades developing accessible strategies to make art a useful tool for real-world social change. As the UK's first Professor of Useful Art, he combines active participation in local, national and international useful art projects with a practical and academic interest in ground-up activism and community empowerment. In an era of rising populism and political polarisation, his research offers essential insights into how we might imagine and remake ourselves otherwise - insights brought together in his 2026 book, Useful Art: How activist artists can change the world. Since 2020, has chaired/co-chaired the Advisory Board of Tŷ Pawb, Wrexham's hybrid market, cultural hub, gallery and community garden - grounded in what Byrne terms 'Cultural Sustainability'. From 2019, Researcher and Writer in Residence at The Whitworth Art Gallery, Manchester, where he co-produced the online research platform Decentralising Political Economies (dpe.tools), linking The Whitworth, the Association of Arte Útil and LJMU's IAT. Earlier, coordinated the ‘Constituencies’ research strand in the L'Internationale Consortium of Museum and Galleires EU-funded project The Uses of Art: The Legacy of 1848 and 1989 (2013–2018).

Thomas is a Senior Lecturer at the School of Cybernetics, at the Australian National University (ANU). He integrates his background in systems engineering and interests in organisational design to research and deploy methods to create safe, sustainable, and responsible systems. His approaches draw on cybernetics, visual arts, and playcentric and embodied methods, to support diverse participants in imagining and acting towards hopeful futures. His current research program develops and evaluates Gameful Experiences for Hopeful Futures. He has applied these approaches in various contexts and at various scales, including a Sino-French joint research lab on haematology in Shanghai; the science diplomacy sections of French embassies in the USA and Australia; and the Australian Higher Education sector. Prior to his current role, he has served as inaugural manager of the 3AI Innovation Institute at ANU, and inaugural program manager for the ANU-wide decarbonisation program, Below Zero. Thomas enjoys combining analysis and his systems engineering training with the creativity and joyfulness of visual arts and gameful design to support major societal transformations.

Benny Corvers co-owns (with Lien Peeters) Prepared Mind, a Belgian-Dutch consultancy firm. Both originally trained as linguists and have worked in the field of organisational design and development for the past 15 years. The Viable System Model and Modern Sociotechnical Systems have been at the core of their work ever since they started out. Benny supports organisations as a strategist, adviser and source of inspiration in complex transformations. He knows how to mobilize groups of people and is always looking for authentic partnerships with his clients. In his previous career, he built teams of people and became fascinated by the magic of high-performing organisations. Prepared Mind’s ambition is to change the world of work by enabling a fundamentally different dialogue within and between organisations, helping clients to design and develop new conditions that will allow their organisations to adjust sustainably. Prepared Mind mainly works with governments and social purpose organisations in youth care, mental health care, education.

Dr Maurizio Tomasella is a Reader and the Deputy Head of Management Science and Business Economics at the University of Edinburgh Business School. Previously at the University of Cambridge Engineering Department (Institute for Manufacturing, Distributed Information and Automation Lab, AutoID Lab) and Politecnico di Milano (Department of Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Systems and Technology Lab). Much of Maurizio's earlier work (2002-2012) looked at enhancing industrial decision making and control by embedding Radio-Frequency IDentification (RFID) and Automatic Identification and Data capture (AutoID) technologies. In 2010, Maurizio was a Core Editor of the first Strategic Research Agenda on the Internet of Things (IoT), on behalf of the European Commission.

Currently studying Global Sustainability Science at Copernicus Institute, Leon Bellin is a writer, artist, and programmer with a background in game development as well as data analysis and collection for climate activism. Due to his first-hand experience in activism and organizing, he knows how useful system approaches are in creating scalable and resilient social movements, properties he thinks many of its contemporary manifestations can improve on. Next to his studies, Leon therefore seeks and practices methods to bring social collectives closer to sustainable behaviors of learning and operating.

affiliation: Bayes Business School, City, University of London
bio: Professor of Information Management at Bayes Business School, City, University of since 1988. His background is in accounting and technology, latterly with active development of arts-based engagement in management studies. He has led large EU and UK funded projects on technology, knowledge and management education. Director of the Bayes Learning Laboratory since 2003, this has involved many initiatives and collaborations in educational innovation, including reflective journaling for leadership, learning by wandering around (the dérive), and novel learning spaces: physical, virtual and imaginative. His interest in roleplay simulations began with paper-based, which has evolved through VLE- based into generative AI based simulations. With colleague Martin Rich, in 2018 Clive won a “most innovative pedagogy of the year” award from the International Management of Organisational Behaviour Teaching Society for the dérive. He is co-founder of the Centre for Creativity for Professional Practice at City, which created the unique multi-disciplinary Masters in Innovation, Creativity and Leadership. The Worshipful Company of Information Technologists is the City of London’s 100th Livery company, and Clive is a founding liveryman and was a member of the Court. He is author of a large number of publications, and lectures, broadcasts and consults in the UK and internationally.

Miguel Garcia Matas is a PhD candidate at the University of Edinburgh, currently at the VIVA stage, specialising in Financial Technology. His industrial PhD thesis examined the intersection of two-sided markets and tokenomics, using a cybernetic approach to develop agent-based simulations for analysing platform viability and governance. He also teaches Economics for Business and Principles of Management at the undergraduate level.

affiliation: Xavier Institute of Management, XIM University
bio: Amar KJR Nayak is a Professor of Strategy and Chairperson of AIESS Centre, Xavier Institute of Management, XIM University, and President, AIESS Society, Bhubaneswar, India. He also chairs the AIESS Global Consortium, and is VP, International Federation for Systems ResearchIn his over three decades of engagements in field/action research and policy formulations to resolve complex problems in reality, Amar founded the All Interacting Evolving Systems Science (AIESS) that explains the phenomena of change, whether regeneration or degeneration, in reality. He also developed the Ecosystemic Transdisciplinary Action Research (ESTAR) Methodology to operationalize Regenerative & Flourishing Ecosystems. The axiology of nothingness of any individual entity in a system, while recognizing the complementary role of every entity in a system, with the weakest other-centered intentionality (WOCI) in a system, are the foundations to Balance and Coherence to his Regenerative Ecosystemic Science. While he has adopted several methodologies from reductionist to systemic methodologies to study and resolve issues in ten different economic-political-social-ecological dimensions/systems/sectors, he primarily adopts ESTAR in his current pursuits towards regenerative living, education, design, and operationalizing regenerative ecosystems in the fast degenerating natural, rural, urban, and industrial ecosystems.

Chris Hamlin, FREng Co-founder and lead advisor at HancockHamlin, a company focused on amplifying the role of engineering and equipping people to operate effectively in complex and emergent environments. A strong consulting professional with more than 30 years’ experience and a track record of improving manufacturing performance and commercial operations across the process industries, Chris is also a Fellow of the Royal Academy of Engineering.  He sits on their Regional Talent Engineering Steering Group and chairs that activity in the North-East. He is a qualified Co-Active Coach, Viable System Model Coach and Emergenetics Practitioner. He has expertise in helping individuals and organisations understand themselves and the systems they are in and how to make sustainable changes that bring personal, professional and societal benefits.

Sascha Kullak is an independent practitioner of applied cybernetics, working at the intersection of urban development and organisational self-governance, based in Münster, Germany. Since 2015, he has co-founded and co-governed B-Side Münster — a commons-public-partnership cultural centre developed through ten years of lived self-organisation. From 2019 to 2024, he orchestrated Hansaforum Münster, a federally funded model project for democratic neighbourhood governance. It was during this time that he became painfully aware of the lack of a self-organisation system as simple to apply as it is potent in effect.c He holds an M.A. in Nonprofit Management, with a thesis on the transfer of Christopher Alexander's Fundamental Differentiating Process to non-profit organisations — which was also the scholarly birth of his heart project: a VSM-based serious game that puts the power of self-organisation into as many people's pockets as possible. He currently works as 'common good officer' (for lack of a better translation) at the Montag Foundation Urban Spaces in Bonn, where he enables a public-interest concept-based tender process for the allocation of real estate to the best idea instead of the highest-bidder.

Ivo is an independent consultant and author. For the past 30 years, he has advised large public and private organisations on their strategy, structure, and knowledge. He is the author of the books Essential Balances and Personal Knowledge Graphs, as well as numerous essays and articles. He holds a PhD in Computer Science. Ivo's work draws on cybernetics, complexity science, and cognitive science. His main interests are knowledge management and socio-technical systems. In the first area, he guides projects for implementing knowledge graphs and provides training courses on semantic technologies. In the second area, he works as a governance consultant and strategy advisor. He conducts independent research in both areas. You can find his latest publications at https://www.linkandth.ink .

Jan De Visch is a seasoned consultant and executive coach with decades of experience facilitating complex organizational development processes. As Managing Director of Connect & Transform, he helps organizations make visible where cIvo Velitchkovollaboration, decision-making and ownership block strategic progress, and supports leadership teams in redesigning the governance, roles and structures needed to deal with complexity. His work connects diagnosis, design and transformation: from sensing where responsibilities and boundaries are unclear, to co-creating adaptive structures, leadership practices and ecosystemic forms of collaboration that can sustain future value creation. As a professor at Flanders Business School, he explores one essential question: What drives organizations toward sustainable growth? His approach blends strategic insight with an in-depth understanding of development, enabling leadership teams to align their structures, cultures, and purposes. Jan is the author of 14 books, including the recent Opening the Box: Systems Thinking for Transformational Conversations (2024), Humanizing the Corporation: A Regenerative Leadership Playbook (2025), and The Developmental Practitioner (2025). His work translates cutting-edge developmental research into practical tools for CEOs, change leaders, and facilitators eager to unlock their organization’s full potential. With Jan, transformation is not just a goal — it’s a guided process of becoming.
Dan Davies is a former economist and banker regulator and a current consultant and writer. He is the author of 'The Unaccountability Machine'

Dr. oec. HSG Martin Pfiffner is a renowned expert on organizational and structural issues. He studied at the University of St. Gallen HSG, where he graduated with a doctorate in economics. As an assistant to Professors Peter Groß (Sociology) and Fredmund Malik (Management), he worked his way into system-oriented management theory. Later he studied management cybernetics in Canada and Wales with Professor Stafford Beer. For over 30 years he has worked as a lecturer, trainer and consultant for organizations in the business and non-business sector. Pfiffner is considered one of the world’s leading experts in the practical application of the Viable System Model and Syntegration®. The basis for his work is ‘The Neurology of Business’. This is what he calls the neurology of an organization and this is also the title of his book. In the last three decades, Martin has supported countless economic, public or private organizations in all corners of the world. In various institutions and functions he contributes to the application of the models and methods of management cybernetics such as the ‘Viable System Model’ or ‘Syntegration®’ for the success of companies.

Andrew Pickering is a leading figure in science and technology studies. He taught for many years at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign before returning to England. He retired from the University of Exeter in 2015 and is now an emeritus professor there in the department of sociology, philosophy and anthropology. He has written on topics as diverse as post-World War II particle physics, mathematics, science and industry in the 19th-century, science, technology and warfare in and since WWII, cybernetics, and our relations with nature and the environment. His writings have been translated into several languages, and his books include Constructing Quarks: A Sociological History of Particle Physics (University of Chicago Press, 1984), The Mangle of Practice: Time, Agency and Science (University of Chicago Press, 1995), The Cybernetic Brain: Sketches of Another Future (University of Chicago Press, 2010) and, most recently, emActing with the World: Agency in the Anthropocene (Duke University Press, 2025).
Sensemaking for leaders when management stops working. Author of The Tautai Principle · Complexity · Cybernetics

Katharine (Kate) is Member of Pi Sigma Alpha, the Political Science Honor Society of the United States, holding a BA (with honors) in Political Science, with studies in biochemistry, two MSc degrees, one in Urban Policy Analysis and Management (with honors) and the other in Environmental Engineering (by research), and a PhD in Ecological Political Economy. She is an alumnus Marie Curie Intra-European Fellow and completed her Habilitation in Resource Economics in 2018, with the Life Sciences Faculty of the Humboldt Universität zu Berlin. She is lead author of over 20 high impact academic articles concerning ecological economics, environmental governance, sustainability, Wicked Problems, and the complexities of life and has led the production of several high impact edited collections and research projects.  She has worked as a senior researcher and/or lecturer at universities throughout Europe and in Asia and the Americas and is currently a staff lecturer with Universidad ECCI (Escuela Colombiana de Carreras Industriales), a member of the research group GEAAD - Grupo Economía, Ambiente y Alternativas al Desarrollo of the Universidad Nacional de Colombia and an adjunct postgraduate supervisor with the Centro Interdisciplinario de Estudios sobre el Desarrollo, of the Universidad de los Andes, Colombia.

Ed van der Winden works is a Dutch IT architect with a degree in computer science from the Technical University of Delft.  He is the chair of the Dutch chapter of SCIO (Systems and Complexity in Organizations) as well as the chair of the Interest Group for system thinking within the KNVI (which translates as the Royal Dutch Society for Information Professionals). He uses systems thinking to improve collaboration and governance within large, bureaucratic organizations with a bottom-up approach.

Robin Asby is a writer and researcher, and a retired academic, entrepreneur, and consultant, author of ‘Thinking Systems: an organic language of harmony for human survival‘, published by Triachy Press in 2021. I obtained a degree in Mathematics from Cambridge University (1965), and a PhD from London University in Mathematical Physics (1968). In my career I have held posts in a number of UK universities and one in the United States. I spent 16 years training teachers, and have also worked for a short time in information technology. My major research interest has been in the development of understanding of Systems Thinking, and its underpinning philosophy. I am currently working on two projects. The first of these projects is to investigate how we can build a truly democratic governing system; that is a governing system to which everyone can contribute and which uses everyone’s expertise. The second project is to better explain the central thesis of my book, which is that Western Society has eschewed process thinking to its detriment.

Carola Ritzinger-Roll is a strategy and sustainability manager, management cybernetics practitioner, and doctoral researcher specialising in organisational design, integrated management systems, and Stafford Beer’s Viable System Model (VSM). Drawing on more than 20 years of experience in industrial organisations, she combines systems thinking with Lean Management and management system practice in highly complex and regulated environments. Her doctoral research at the University of Stuttgart investigates how cybernetic performance measurement can improve organisational steering and translate the principles of viable organisation into measurable governance structures. She is co-author of Designing Intelligent Construction Projects (Wiley, 2022) and has published on the application of management cybernetics and the VSM across different industries. Alongside her industrial and academic work, she teaches management-related subjects and is actively involved in the systems and cybernetics community.

Louis is a Senior Associate at pims.ai | malik, based in the firm’s London office and working in its Predictive Analytics practice. His work centres on evidence-based strategy: using six decades of PIMS data to give organisations an objective assessment of their operational and strategic position, and to ground customer and market decisions in empirical benchmarks rather than internal assumption. More recently he has focused on a quantitative reworking of Stafford Beer’s operations room. Where Beer’s design expressed performance as a triple index of Actuality, Capability and Potentiality but could set its reference points only from within the system, Louis’s work anchors them externally — drawing on the PIMS evidence base to show a business what comparable firms have achieved from a similar position, and giving the operations room an external empirical grounding that Beer. It situates the PIMS models within the management-cybernetics tradition of the Viable System Model and the St Gallen lineage behind Malik Management. Louis holds an MSc in Management from the London School of Economics.

Angus Jenkinson is retired full research professor whose research domain was the individualisation of value propositions by coherent enterprises. He was also influential as a tech and business designer and strategic consultant in this field. He has created multiple tools including Virtuoso, a coherent identity frame. He is a Life Fellow of the Cybernetics Society and its former Secretary revitalising its mission. He cooperates as a research fellow of Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) and in Thinking.Institute.

affiliation: Department of Economics, Management, Institutions, University of Naples Federico II
bio: Fabiana Sepe, PhD, is an assistant professor at the Department of Economics, Management, Institutions, University of Naples Federico II. She is author of some book chapters and articles on national and international journals in the fields of management, tourism, and agri-food industry. She has attended several national and international conferences with co-authored papers. Her main research interests include but are not limited to knowledge management, strategy, consumer behaviour and artificial intelligence, concentrating upon the application of open innovation perspectives.

affiliation: Department of Economics, Management, and Institutions (DEMI) of the University of Naples
bio: Francesco Caputo, Ph.D., is an Associate Professor of Business Management at the Department of Economics, Management, and Institutions (DEMI) of the University of Naples Federico II. He is the President of ASVSA (Association for Research on Viable Systems) and Co-Director General of WOSC (World Organization of Systems and Cybernetics). He serves on the editorial boards of numerous international scientific journals and acts as a reviewer for several Italian and international journals. He was a finalist for the 2012/2013 Emerald/EMRBI Business Research Award and has received numerous scientific accolades, including the Tenth Most Cited Article in 2019 JOB Impact Factor Award, the Best Paper Award at the 10th Naples Forum on Service, and the Best Paper Nomination at the 9th International Conference IESS 2018. He is the author of over 180 publications, including books, scientific articles, conference proceedings, and abstracts. His main research interests include, among others, complexity, knowledge management, and systems thinking.
